title: Handling Cookies, Sessions & Forms 🍪
description: Maintain login sessions, submit forms, and bypass simple CSRF protections – the key to web automation.

slides.title: Why Sessions?
slides.content:
# Persistence Across Requests

Websites use cookies to maintain state (logged‑in user, shopping cart). If you send separate `requests.get()`, each is independent. You need a **Session** to automatically handle cookies.

```python
s = requests.Session()
s.get('https://example.com/login')      # gets initial cookie
s.post('https://example.com/login', data=credentials)  # sends cookie
```

slides.title: Session Example
slides.content: Login and then access a protected page:
slides.codeSnippet:
import requests
s = requests.Session()
# Simulated login (use httpbin for testing)
login_resp = s.post('https://httpbin.org/post', data={'user':'admin','pass':'1234'})
# Now access a page that would be behind auth
profile = s.get('https://httpbin.org/get')
print(profile.json())

quizData.question: A `requests.Session` object automatically stores and sends cookies set by the server.
quizData.explanation: Sessions persist cookies across requests, just like a browser.

slides.title: Submitting a Form with CSRF Token
slides.content:
# Step‑by‑Step Automation

1. GET the login page.
2. Parse the CSRF token from the form.
3. POST the login credentials + CSRF token.
4. Check if login succeeded (redirect, welcome message).

```python
s = requests.Session()
# Step 1: get page
login_page = s.get('https://example.com/login')
soup = BeautifulSoup(login_page.text, 'html.parser')
# Step 2: extract token
token_input = soup.find('input', {'name': 'csrf_token'})
token = token_input['value']
# Step 3: submit
payload = {'username': 'admin', 'password': 'secret', 'csrf_token': token}
resp = s.post('https://example.com/login', data=payload)
if 'Welcome' in resp.text:
    print('Login successful')
```

quizData.question: Why do you need to extract a CSRF token before submitting a login form?

options.text: To increase security of the form
Because the server will reject the POST without a valid token

quizData.explanation: CSRF tokens are anti‑CSRF measures; the server verifies it's present and correct.

slides.title: Handling Cookies Manually
slides.content:
# You Can Also Send Cookies Explicitly

```python
cookies = {'sessionid': 'abcd1234'}
resp = requests.get(url, cookies=cookies)
```
Or read `Set-Cookie` from responses and pass them along. But Sessions do this automatically.

slides.title: Browser DevTools are Your Friend
slides.content:
# Reverse Engineer the Requests

Open Chrome DevTools (Network tab), perform the action manually, and look at the exact request: URL, method, headers, form data. Then replicate it in Python.

This is how you automate anything – from liking a post to scraping protected data.

slides.title: Terms of Service & Ethics
slides.content:
## Always check robots.txt and ToS before scraping or automating

Unauthorised access or scraping can be illegal. Use only on sites you own or have explicit permission. Bug bounty programs often allow it within scope.

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Use `requests.Session` with `mount` for retries

```python
from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
s = requests.Session()
s.mount('https://', HTTPAdapter(max_retries=3))
```
Makes your tool resilient to intermittent failures.
